leads.name: The Forster Linde
leads.access: Free. Stands on a public street (Forster Linde) in the Aachen-Forst district, beside a church and a former courthouse; fenced for root protection but visible and reachable on foot, no ticket or appointment needed.
leads.transport: Aachen-Forst, roughly 15-20 minutes by bus from Aachen Hauptbahnhof (exact stop not verified this pass).
leads.verify_notes: Bomenbieb.nl lead ('linde aken', planted band 1300-1500, tagged species_nl 'hollandse-linde') gave the coordinate and address only, per the facts-only licence; both independent sources used here are the City of Aachen's own municipal page and German Wikipedia, both fetched and read directly (not bomenbieb). SPECIES CONFLICT: bomenbieb tags it as Common Lime ('hollandse-linde'/Tilia x europaea) but both the city of Aachen's own page and de.wikipedia consistently call it a Winterlinde (Tilia cordata, Small-leaved Lime); went with the two independently-agreeing sources over the register tag. Widely reported as the oldest tree in Aachen. AGE: not a documented planting date, it's a repeated estimate: garden architect Prince Puckler-Muskau assessed it at 'more than 800 years' on a visit in 1852; both sources repeat this and note the exact age cannot be pinned down, so treat 'roughly 1,000 years' as the vague-source estimate carried forward roughly 174 years, not a precise figure. GIRTH: sources disagree slightly, city page says 10 m trunk circumference, Wikipedia says 9.5 m at the base; used 950 cm (the more specific/frequently cited base measurement) and noted the range here. STORY MATERIAL: five major stems fork from the base about 2-3 m up, formed roughly 300 years ago when the original main stem broke off in the crown; local tradition holds it was a 'Gerichtslinde' (court linden) of the Schonforst domain, where judgments including capital sentences were passed until 1390, with executions carried out nearby at the 'Galgenpley' (gallows field); a restored medieval Schoffenhaus (magistrates' house) still stands beside it. Post-war repairs filled hollow sections with concrete, a now-outdated arboricultural practice, per de.wikipedia. Officially a protected Naturdenkmal (natural monument) for over 30 years, regularly inspected, crown stabilised with cables. SINGLE-TREE-DESTINATION CANDIDATE: Aachen has no Ancient Trees page. This tree is widely described as the city's oldest tree, carries its own Wikipedia article, an official municipal page with a QR-code interpretive trail, and a real history; it clears the single-famous-tree exception (2026-08-31 ruling) on its own. Awaiting a place/page decision; not published by this pass.
